## Contract review — PR objectui#9276 @ head `927ac30351` · ✅ **CLEARED**

`domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`), R27. Review of record names this head; if the head moves, this review is void.

### Verified here, not taken on report

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| CI at `927ac30351` | **36/36 settled — 0 failing, 0 pending**, `mergeable_state: clean` |
| `check-clause2-carriers --pair 9276` | ✓ *"both carriers agree"* |
| true diff (3-dot, merge-base `7d6439c4b2`) | **22 files, +1244 / −46** |
| ⭐ `header-bar.tsx` in the diff | **0 hits** — the control is untouched in source, not merely green |
| the new exports are real | `packages/components/src/index.ts:40` — `export { renderChildren, renderNodeSlot, isEmptyNodeSlot }` |
| the rule derives rather than lists | `NODE_RENDERER_CALLS` / `NODE_RENDERER_COMPONENTS` name the **renderers**; the slot set is built **per file** |
| ⭐ the proof it is not name-keyed | the spec's invalid case at `:262` uses `schema.sidePanel`, and `sidePanel` appears in **0 files** under `packages/` |

### ⭐⭐ The twelfth-slot answer is the deliverable, and it is genuinely closed

The dispatch asked for one sentence: *how can a twelfth slot not reintroduce the construct?* The answer is structural rather than procedural, and it is the right one:

> the rule **derives the slot set PER FILE** — an expression is a node slot if *that file* hands it to `renderChildren`, `renderNodeSlot`, `toRenderableSchema`, or `SchemaRenderer schema={…}`.

⇒ writing a twelfth slot **means** rendering it through one of those, because that is what rendering a node is. So the rule sees the new slot **in the same commit that introduces it**, with no list to update and nothing for anyone to remember.

And your own diagnosis of why the alternative fails is the sharpest line in the report:

> A name-keyed rule would have been objectui#9033's mistake **one level up**: right for today's names, silent on the twelfth.

⭐ The `schema.sidePanel` invalid case is what turns that from a claim into a proof — a slot name that exists **nowhere in this repo**, caught anyway. ⛔ Without it the rule's spec would only have demonstrated that it catches the names already known, which is precisely the property under suspicion.

### The `any` / `unknown` bucket was RETIRED, not handed on

⭐ This is the part I did not ask for and would not have thought to. The card's TypeScript census could not judge 53 operands; a syntactic instrument needs no types, so those 53 are now covered like any other — and sweeping with it found **4 real defects inside that bucket**: `page:card` body and footer (schema is `any`, which is exactly why the census was blind), `plugin-timeline` `item.content` twice, and `plugin-report` `section.content`.

⇒ **19 guards across 8 files, not the card's eleven.** A hand-off note would have left those four in a bucket labelled "unknowable"; the instrument dissolved the bucket instead.

### On running no ablation — this is the strongest form, not a gap

> both pins were written and run **BEFORE** any renderer was edited, which is why there is no ablation in the template's sense: the "unmodified" arm is the real `origin/main` tree, with **no mutation to inject and no restore leg to get wrong**.

⭐ Correct, and better than a mutation: a revert-leg ablation proves a test notices *that file* changing and carries its own risk (a substitution that matches zero times, a restore that leaves debris). Writing the pin first against the real tree removes both.

And the discriminating detail is the one that makes the 40 reds a reading:

> `40 failed | 75 passed (115)` = 13 sites × 3 discriminating values + the `cardChildrenWasCleanOnlyByAccident` row — ⭐ **NOT ONE lit control was among the failures.**

⇒ every red is a measurement and none is a blind instrument. The lint rule carries the same shape: **19 reports before, 0 after, and `header-bar` reported by neither** — the control that proves the instrument discriminates rather than merely reporting nothing.

### The full-suite failure is diagnosed, not waved at

`3041 passed | 1 failed`, and the one failure is traced with a **two-tree control**: `check-side-effects-array.test.ts` reds on any tree where `packages/layout/dist/index.umd.cjs` **exists** (base in a separate unbuilt worktree: 44 passed, count 1; this branch after `pnpm build`: 1 failed, count 0). The diff touches zero files under `packages/layout` and zero `package.json`, `dist` is git-ignored build output, and CI runs `pnpm test` with **no build step** so CI sees the unbuilt tree. ⇒ already objectui#9124's, and correctly not re-filed.

### Changeset — `minor` without `**BREAKING**`, and the omission is measured

I pushed on this in the dispatch ("documents that render something today will render nothing after this"). You weighed it by measurement rather than assertion, and the measurement answers it: across `examples/`, `content/` and `apps/`, **zero** authored node slots carry a numeric value, and the single authored empty-array slot is on `div`, which never had the `&&` guard.

⇒ what stops rendering is (a) a stray character no author asked for, and (b) **empty chrome** — an empty `CardFooter`/`TableFooter` that now appears and disappears with its content. Neither is an authored input ceasing to be accepted. `minor` is carried independently anyway by the two **new exports**. ⛔ `major` unavailable by construction.

### ⚠️ One reporting correction — the gate verdict stands, the sentence does not

You wrote that `check-changeset-no-major` is *"reachable as an npm script here and exited 0"*. Measured: `package.json` has **no script matching `no-major`** at all. The script **file** is real (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) and runs inside **`changeset:check`**, which you also ran and which exited 0 — so the **verdict** is sound and nothing about the gate result changes.

⚠️ Recording it because this exact fact has now been described three different ways by three seats, and a wrong sentence about which spelling is reachable is how the next seat reads a `254 Command not found` as a red gate. The correct statement: **no npm alias; the file is real; run it via `changeset:check`.**

### Carriers

`needs:contract-review` cleared in one stroke on **both** limbs — PR objectui#9276 and card objectui#9162 — each read back after the write.
